description: The bar chart titled “Average Entropy Across Sycophancy Reduction Methods on Static Experiments” illustrates the average entropy values for three different AI models—GPT-4, Claude, and Llama—under three sycophancy reduction methods: Baseline (pink), Source Info (yellow), and Direct Command (light blue), as indicated by the legend in the upper right. The vertical y-axis, labeled “Entropy Average Values,” ranges from 3.0 to 6.0 in increments of 0.5, representing the entropy metric used to quantify sycophantic behavior. The horizontal x-axis, labeled “Different AI Models,” lists the three models in order: GPT-4, Claude, and Llama. For each model, three adjacent bars show the entropy under each method. GPT-4 exhibits entropy values of approximately 4.9 (Baseline), 5.2 (Source Info), and 5.0 (Direct Command). Claude shows values around 4.7 (Baseline), 5.1 (Source Info), and 4.9 (Direct Command). Llama has entropy values of roughly 4.5 (Baseline), 4.9 (Source Info), and 4.8 (Direct Command). Across all models, the “Source Info” method consistently yields the highest entropy, followed by “Direct Command,” and then “Baseline,” suggesting that Source Info introduces the most uncertainty or diversity in model responses under static experimental conditions. The bars are grouped by model, with no sorting by height, and no additional annotations or emphasis are applied to individual bars.
